# Summary of University of the Andes (Colombia)
The University of the Andes (Universidad de los Andes or Uniandes) was founded in 1948 as Colombia’s first nonsectarian and politically independent university, officially commencing classes in March 1949 with 80 students. Modeled after American universities, it sought to produce professionals and leaders aligned with Colombia’s modernization amid social and political change. Early focus included humanities, sciences, and technical education, with innovative programs such as a three/two system allowing students to complete part of their studies domestically before transferring to U.S. institutions. Despite Colombia’s political violence in the 1950s, Uniandes maintained political neutrality through inclusive governance involving members from major political parties and military connections. The university actively recruited foreign and national professors and organized prestigious academic conferences. It achieved university status in 1964.
Governance is overseen by a Board of Trustees (30-45 members including professors and students) and a Board of Directors responsible for development plans and management. The Rector, Vice-Rectors, Deans, and Academic Council manage academic and administrative issues. The university comprises 14 academic units including 10 faculties and specialized centers, employing mainly full-time faculty with about 70% holding PhDs from top global universities. The student body is competitive, with 95% of undergraduates ranking in the top 1% nationally, a balanced gender ratio, and substantial enrollment from outside Bogotá. Uniandes promotes interdisciplinary studies and hosts exchange programs with over 119 universities in 34 countries.
Financially, the university possesses significant assets valued at over US$400 million (2020 figures), supporting its strategic autonomy and growth. Its mission emphasizes pluralism, dialogue, academic excellence, ethical formation, and social responsibility aimed at addressing Colombia’s challenges.
